newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Norwegian named U.N. representative in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian named U.N. representative in Bosnia.

text.p: Norwegian diplomat Kai Eide is to become the new U.N. special representative in Bosnia-Herzegovina, a U.N. spokesman said on Friday.
He will succeed Iqbal Riza of Pakistan, recently appointed chef de cabinet of the new U.N. secretary-general, Kofi Annan.

Eide, 47, served most recently as a special adviser on Balkan affairs in the Norwegian foreign ministry. From 1993 to 1995 he was an envoy to the international conference on the former Yugoslavia and before that was Norway's deputy permanent representative to NATO in Brussels.

The United Nations has a 1,700-member International Police Task Force in Bosnia-Herzegovina where a Stabilisation Force (SFOR) comprising about 32,000 troops from NATO and non-NATO countries is helping implement the 1995 Dayton peace accords.
The United Nations also announced the appointment of Manfred Seitner of Denmark as the new commissioner of the International Police Task Force.

Seitner, 53, currently operational head of the Danish national security and intelligence service, will take up his new post on March 3, succeeding Patrick Fitzgerald of Ireland who has completed his tour of duty.
